scenario: QUIET_CLAMP: payload@90, payload@91, ONE internal-tracker tick @122, then silence; the chain advances to 136 behind retention floor 130 — the replay window evicted slots 92..129 (38 slots).
question: PULS 4 proved the age-out reservation holds for ANY slot cursor. This measurement asks the open design question the thread left: does the SDK's own documented consumer-side repair actually work, and what does it cost?
repair_pieces_tested: LaserstreamClient::subscribe_replay_info() -> first_available (the SDK's own unary RPC; its docstring says: clamp with from_slot.max(first_available))
subscribe_with_options(..., SubscribeOptions::default().with_intra_slot_updates(true)) — turns the silent OUT_OF_RANGE retry loop into a TERMINAL consumer error
a fresh subscribe() with from_slot = first_available (the clamp) plus a locally declared gap

silent.meaning: default options: the consumer sees ZERO errors while the SDK retries the refused 122 forever — the stall PULS 4 found, on the harder chain-advanced shape

intra.meaning: intra_slot_updates=true: the consumer SEES the terminal OutOfRange — the SDK already owns the switch that makes the stall loud

repair.meaning: on the terminal error the consumer queries subscribe_replay_info (first_available=130), re-subscribes with from_slot=130, resumes live delivery at the floor, and DECLARES 92..129 as a gap — 38 slots named instead of silently vanished

control.meaning: the false-positive guard: the same repair WITHOUT the clamp (fresh subscribe at the stale cursor 122) is refused AGAIN — the clamp is what makes the repair work, not the re-subscribe alone

findings: The repair is real and entirely consumer-side: no SDK change, no server change. Three SDK pieces the SDK already ships (replay_info + intra_slot_updates + explicit from_slot) turn the silent infinite stall into a declared gap plus live delivery.

The cost is honest and permanent: slots 92..129 (38 slots) are unrecoverable — the repair can name them, never refill them. What the clamp buys is truth (a declared, machine-readable gap) instead of silence.

The unclamped control shows the re-subscribe alone is NOT the repair: at the stale cursor the server refuses again. max(cursor, first_available) is the operative rule — exactly what the SDK's own replay-info docstring prescribes.
Default options make the repair UNREACHABLE in practice: the consumer never sees an error, so it never knows to repair. intra_slot_updates is the switch that connects the stall to the repair.
falsification_guards: silent cell must show 0 consumer errors (the stall is invisible)
intra cell must show >=1 consumer error (the error is surfaced)
repair cell must show exactly 1 replay_info query, first_available=130, clamp_from=130, >=5 delivered slots after the clamp, gap_declared_range_size=38
control cell must be refused again (>0 OUT_OF_RANGE) and deliver 0 slots (no clamp, no repair)
regression: All eight 2026-11-20 quiet-matrix cells (rule x window x options) reproduce IDENTICAL values after the harness extension (only three additive diagnostic keys: chain_head_harness, first_available_reported, replay_info_queries); the quiet matrix summary is byte-identical; the 2026-11-19 variant-A cell was spot-checked byte-identical and restored from its pristine copy.
limits: mock geyser: window = a single retention floor + a chain head; real LaserStream retention/eviction pacing approximated, not measured against live infrastructure
Rust SDK only (2.0.0 from crates.io for main, PR #114 vendored verbatim for the pr114 rule); #115 names the same cursor logic in the Go and JS SDKs
the declared gap is the consumer's own bookkeeping — the SDK has no gap primitive; a real repair would record it in the consumer's durable state (reeflog's gap ledger is exactly this shape)
subscribe_replay_info between stall and repair races eviction: a real server's floor can move between the query and the fresh subscribe
